1Purpose

This policy is the frame for the module at [Provider name]. It names the seven standards we work to and the policy that carries each one, the roles that run the module, and the rules that apply across the whole module. It sets no time limit and restates no commitment of its own: each of POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 holds its commitments, its clocks and its checks in one place. It is for families, our workers, the other services in a child's team, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us, and their , from first contact until end.
  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] and has contact with those children or families: employees, contractors, students, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every place we work: the family home, early learning and school settings, community places, our premises, and phone or video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership registered for these supports, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy is the shared frame for the module. POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 each set out one standard in full, with its own commitments, times and checks; nothing in this policy changes them. POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy sets the child safety rules for all our work with children; until it is written, the appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule.

3Commitments

C1

We will do what POL-ECS-02 The Child Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the child, s 56).

C2

We will do what POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the family, s 57).

C3

We will do what POL-ECS-04 Inclusion Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (inclusion, s 58).

C4

We will do what POL-ECS-05 Collaboration Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (collaboration, s 59).

C5

We will do what POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (capacity building, s 60).

C6

We will do what POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (evidence-informed supports, s 61).

C7

We will do what POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (outcome based approach, s 62).

4Ground rules

G1

A child's safety comes before everything else in this policy. A worker who is worried about a child acts on that worry first.

G2

A person with decides about the child's supports. We ask for the child's own views in a way that fits their age and how they communicate, and we record them.

G3

One route for every concern. A practice concern goes to the . A conduct or safety concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or an owner goes to the chair of the governing body, or in a sole trader's business to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A child who may be at goes to the the same day, under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). The person a concern is about never handles it.

G4

The time limits of the module are set in POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 and the procedures under them; the Module clocks table at the end of these ground rules reproduces them, and this policy sets none of its own. Where the law sets a shorter time, the shorter time applies.

G5

The appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule: the law of [state or territory] on who must report, the test, where, how fast, and the duty of every adult to tell police of child sexual abuse. POL-CHS-01, when written, holds the wider child safe standards and reportable conduct rules. The Quality Manager checks the schedule every 12 months and when the law changes.

G6

Each fact is held once. REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is the one register for the module and holds dates, names, counts and record numbers. The forms hold the detail and the family's words.

G7

A family can say no to a , a referral, a team meeting or a question. Saying no is recorded and is never a reason to reduce supports.

G8

A complaint made by a child or family at any point is handled under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. A child's "stop" or "not happy" signal is a complaint the child can make in their own way.

G9

A sole trader holds every role except practice supervisor and independent contact for concerns. An outside practice supervisor with early childhood experience and the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register are the checks on the sole trader's own work.

G10

The is the practitioner accountable for the child's and the register row. Where the family chooses a key worker from our team, the key worker is the plan lead, and when the key worker changes the plan-lead role moves with it the same day.

9Words we use

345 words
early childhood supports
supports for a young child with developmental delay or disability, and their family, under the registration class "early intervention supports for early childhood".
family
the parents, carers and other people who raise the child, as the family itself describes them.
parental responsibility
the legal authority to make decisions for a child. A court or child protection order can change who holds it.
support network
the relatives, friends, educators and others in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.
everyday routines
the things the child does most days, such as meals, play, bath time, getting dressed and going to early learning.
key worker
the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker, that person is the plan lead.
team around the child
the family, our practitioners and the other providers who work together on the child's plan.
plan lead
the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.
practice supervisor
the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners.
practitioner drafting for the plan lead
the practitioner the plan lead asks to draft the plan under PRO-ECS-08. The plan lead stays accountable for the plan.
functional outcome
something the child will do in daily life, written so the family can see when it has happened.
coaching
helping a parent, carer or educator practise a strategy in their own routine, in place of doing it for them.
both clearances
an NDIS worker screening clearance, and the working with children check of [state or territory].
child safety lead
the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.
risk of harm
the words this module uses for the reporting threshold. Our test is that you suspect on reasonable grounds that a child is at risk of harm. The appendix to POL-ECS-02 gives the exact term used in [state or territory].
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

1Purpose

The result: every child has a written that the has said is theirs. It names what will change in daily life, what each person will do, and how we will measure it. The family has a copy they can use, and hears how things are going in their own way.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood ), C1 to C13.

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • the family has accepted our offer and the first session is held: step 1 opens the ( 0) within 10 of the first session, and steps 1 to 21 make the first full plan as the is under way
  • a is due, at least every 3 months after approval (steps 22 to 24)
  • a is due (steps 25 and 26)
  • a is due, or a trigger in Decision table 4 happens (steps 27 and 28)
  • the monthly and 6 monthly checks fall due (steps 29 and 30).

Who acts:

  • The writes the plan with the family and runs every check, report and review. Where the family chose a of ours, that person is the plan lead. Where the plan lead asks a practitioner to draft a part, that practitioner is the : they work with the family and the plan lead stays accountable. PRO-ECS-03 The Family Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) uses the same role.
  • Every practitioner who works with the child tells the plan lead what they see, and records each session in FRM-ECS-05 Session Record.
  • The Service Manager approves each version of the plan, and checks the register every month.
  • The Quality Manager reads the results for all children every 6 months.

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds every role. At step 16 a sole trader checks their own plan against Decision table 2 and signs it. The independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register reads a sample of 3 plans every 6 months.

A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

A question number such as Q4 means a question in FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, unless another form is named.

In this procedure, T0 means the day the Service Manager signs the child's assessment under PRO-ECS-04 Inclusion Procedure (Early Childhood Supports), step 26. For a later version, T0 is the day of the plan review. The interim plan (version 0) does not wait for T0: it is agreed within 10 business days of the first session.

The is one of achieved, progressing, no change or gone back. Q30 of FRM-ECS-07 says how to choose it.

3Before you start

  • You are named as the plan lead in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register, col D.
  • For a first plan, the family record FRM-ECS-02 and the assessment FRM-ECS-03 are under way. You can draft before the assessment is signed. You cannot approve the plan until it is.
  • You have a blank FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan.
  • You have the family's communication preferences: REG-ECS-01 col G, and FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form if the family made one.
  • You have the consent lines in FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record, questions 7 and 8, for anyone else you will talk to.
  • You can book the interpreter the family chooses.
  • For a check or review, you have the last approved version, the last progress checks and the FRM-ECS-05 entries for the plan period.
  • You have set aside time. Most families more than one conversation. The family sets the pace.

4Watch out

  • A plan approved before the family says it is theirs is not their plan. The family may not use it, and the supports may aim at the wrong things.
  • An outcome about our activity or a test score shows we were busy, not that the child's life changed. The family cannot tell whether things are better.
  • A health strategy written by a worker who is not qualified can injure the child. Only the qualified practitioner writes it.
  • A plan in words the family cannot read is not a copy they can use. They cannot hold us to it, and they may stop taking part.
  • A report that is better than the truth hides a child who needs something different. It also breaches the duty to act with integrity, honesty and transparency (Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(d)).
  • A child, brother or sister who interprets can change what is said. Meaning is lost, and the child carries an adult's worries.
  • A concern that a child is at cannot wait for the plan. Act the same day (step 6). A delay can leave a child unprotected.

5Steps

Open the plan

Step 1

The plan lead

Open a version of the plan and write why it is being made.

Use the child's row in REG-ECS-01. Write the record number, the version number and the reason from Decision table 4. For a new child, open version 0, the interim plan, within 10 business days of the first session: with the family, write one to three starting outcomes in their words (Q9 to Q11), the supports and who does them (Q14), and who agreed (Q3, Q22 and Q23). No yet, and no Service Manager approval: the family's agreement and your signature are enough. Coaching under PRO-ECS-06 Capacity Building Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) starts under it. Then open version 1, the first full plan, as the assessment is under way; it replaces the interim plan when approved. For a later version, start from the last approved version and the progress checks.

Confirm who can agree to this version for the child.

Read REG-ECS-01 col F and FRM-ECS-04 question 2. Ask the person named whether anything has changed. Ask to see any order or agency letter that limits who agrees. The Quality Manager reports any plan more than 20 business days past its review date to the Chief Executive
Someone wants the practitioner to work on something that is not in the planThe practitioner keeps to the approved plan or the interim plan and tells the plan lead the same day. The plan lead starts a review with the family within 5 business days and holds it within 10, using Decision table 4. If the family wants it added, make a new version. The practitioner works on it only when the new version is approved
The practitioner for a support is awayThe Service Manager names a replacement the child knows, as REG-ECS-01 col Y says. The replacement reads the plan before the next session
The plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, or leavesThe Service Manager names another worker within 2 business days. They read the plan and the checks, and tell the family who they are
A check shows a sudden loss of skills, or the family tells you of a health changeTell the family to contact the child's doctor or health practitioner. With consent, tell the practitioner. Hold a review under Decision table 4. Follow step 6 if the child may be at risk
The family disagrees with a report or the result of an assessmentDo not record it as agreed. Write what they say beside ours. Their words stand where the two differ. The Service Manager meets them within 5 business days. Tell them how to complain under PRO-FBK-01
Another provider's report differs from the family's view or oursWrite both views. With consent, ask the provider what they saw. Go through it with the family. Change the plan only with the family
Your concern is about a colleague or a manager, for example a report that says more than was doneA concern about how a colleague practises goes to the . A concern about a colleague's or a manager's conduct, for example a report that says more than was done, goes to the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or the owner, tell the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business, tell the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01. This is the one rule POL-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Policy sets. You can phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
The family complainsHandle it the same day under PRO-FBK-01
The system is downUse the paper form. Enter it in REG-ECS-01 within 1 business day of the system coming back
A sole trader has no Service ManagerCheck the plan against Decision table 2 and sign it. The independent contact reads a sample of 3 plans every 6 months

8Done means

The plan is in place when all of these are true:

  • the family has said the plan is theirs, and the Service Manager has approved it (the interim plan, version 0, needs only the family's agreement)
  • each outcome starts from a family priority or need, names a routine, place and people, and has a starting point and five levels
  • each support has a person, a routine, a place and a start date
  • the family has their copy in the way they chose, and has said back what it says
  • every worker who sees the child has the plan
  • the register shows the plan, the first check date and the next review date.

These records now exist:

  • the completed FRM-ECS-07, with its sign-off, in the participant's file
  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01, with col S, col M, col T, col U, col V, the next check in col AL, and the next due date computed in col AE
  • the lines in FRM-ECS-04 question 29 for any plan shared outside the family
  • after each check, Q29 to Q32 and col V
  • after each report, Q33 and Q34 and col X
  • after each review, Q35 and Q36, and a new version if anything changed.

9Quick card

158 words
  • If you think a child may be at risk of harm, follow PRO-ECS-02 now. Call 000 if there is immediate danger (step 6)
  • Confirm who can agree to the plan before you draft it (step 2)
  • Agree the interim plan with the family within 10 business days of the first session, so coaching can start (step 1)
  • Ask the family which language, mode and terms they understand best (step 3)
  • Write each outcome from a family priority, in their words, in a named routine (step 8)
  • Never write a health strategy yourself. Ask the qualified practitioner (step 13)
  • Do not approve a plan the family has not said is theirs (step 15)
  • Give the copy within 5 business days of approval, in the family's way (step 18)
  • Check each outcome with the family every 3 months, and report progress as it is (step 22)
  • Review the plan at least every 6 months, and at each trigger (step 27)

form.intro:
This is the family record for one child. It holds what the family knows about their child, and their strengths. It also holds what is hard and what they want most. It holds how they learn and live, their culture and community, and how they want to work with us. Every plan starts from it and is checked against it.

Keep one family record for each child. It is built with the family over more than one conversation. Add dated entries and never write over an old one. The family's copy is Sections A to K without question 42: questions 42 and 43 are internal checks and are not given to the family. For an interim plan under PRO-ECS-08, made within 10 of the first session, the core set is questions 2, 5, 7, 9, 10, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 23, 24, 25 and 29; the rest are gathered across the plan period and before the first full plan. "Optional: No" in the tables means we ask the question; the family may still answer any question "chose not to say".

Who completes it:

  • The plan lead completes it with the family, at a time and place the family chooses. A parent or carer can write their own answers instead.
  • The family can bring anyone they like. An interpreter, an advocate or a cultural support person can sit in.
  • The Service Manager completes question 42 (internal, not given to the family).
  • The plan lead completes question 43 at each (internal, not given to the family).

Have ready:

  • the intake answers, FRM-SUP-01 Referral and Intake Form questions 7, 8, 17 and 22, so you ask only what is missing
  • the communication preferences, FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, if the family made one
  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • an interpreter, if the family wants one.

You do not need reports. Ask the family first. The questions are in plain words, so you can ask them aloud. Every question can be answered "chose not to say". That is a real answer and never a gap.

What happens next: PRO-ECS-03 The Family Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The priorities at question 19 go to FRM-ECS-03 Everyday Routines and Participation and FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan. Community and service links the family wants are carried to FRM-ECS-03 Section G, which is their one home. The family gets a copy. The record is reviewed at every plan review and whenever something changes.

form.intro:
This is the team record for one child. It names the and the key worker if the family chose one. It records what the family agreed may be shared, each team meeting and each planned move.

Keep one team record for each child. It stays open while we support the child. Add dated entries. Never write over an old entry.

Who completes it:

  • The Service Manager completes question 1, question 3 and question 41.
  • The plan lead completes the rest of Sections A to D, and Sections G and H, with the family.
  • The plan lead adds one entry to Section E for each team meeting. A key worker of ours may do it with them.
  • Every practitioner of ours adds a line to Section F each time they send or receive a document, or share with a new person.

Have these ready:

  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • nothing else for consent: Section C of this record is the family's consent record for sharing within the team
  • any court order or agency letter about who decides for the child
  • the child's plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, once it is written.

PRO-ECS-05 Collaboration Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The family receives a copy of Sections A to C, of questions 13 to 15 and 17 to 20, and of every meeting entry. Question 16 stays in the file.

Do not write a child protection concern in this record. Use FRM-ECS-01 Child Protection Concern and Report Record. If you do not know an answer, write "not yet asked" and the date. Ask at the next contact with the family.

This statement is for the family.

We collect this information so the people who support your child can work as one team. The NDIS Practice Standards require us to coordinate that team and to share information only with your consent.

Our practitioners who work with your child read this record. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager.

We share your information with a team member only as you agree at question 7. You can say no to any person or any item. Your supports continue either way.

There is one exception. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can ask to see this record and ask us to correct it. You can change or withdraw your consent at any time by telling [contact person]. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.

form.intro:
This is the support plan for one child and their family. It says what will change in the child's and the family's daily life. It also says what each person will do to help, and how we will know it is working. The family keeps a copy. Every worker who sees the child follows it.

The plan is made of . Each one is something the child or the family will do in a routine, a place and with people, which anyone could see or hear. Each outcome has supports, which the Quality Indicators call interventions, and a way of measuring.

Keep one plan for each child. Version 0 is the interim plan: one to three starting outcomes and their supports, agreed with the family within 10 business days of the first session, with no and no Service Manager approval. starts under it. Version 1 is the first full plan and replaces it. A new version is made whenever an outcome, a measure or a support changes. The last approved version stays in force until the new one is approved.

Who completes it:

  • The completes every section except Section B and questions 24 and 25, with the family, at a time and place the family chooses. Where the plan lead asks a practitioner to write a part, the plan lead stays accountable.
  • A parent or carer can write their own answers instead. The family can bring anyone: an interpreter, an advocate or a cultural support person.
  • The practitioner who assesses the child completes Section B. For FRM-ECS-03 that is the plan lead.
  • The Service Manager completes questions 24 and 25.

Have ready:

  • the family record, FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record
  • the assessment, FRM-ECS-03 Everyday Routines and Participation Assessment, and any other assessment report

form.privacy:
This statement is for the family. Read it aloud, in the language and way the family uses.

"We write this plan with you. It says what you want for your child and your family, what each of us will do, and how we will know it is working. We use your words where we can.

You choose what goes in the plan. You can say no to any question and to any part of the plan. Saying no does not reduce your child's supports.

The workers who support your child read this plan. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager. We give the plan to a teacher, an educator or another service only if you agree, and only the parts you agree to.

We write down how your child is going and use it to show you. We do not use it to judge you or your family.

There is one exception. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can read this plan, ask for a copy in the way that suits you, and ask us to correct it at any time. Ask [privacy contact role and contact details]."

Tell an educator or another provider who adds to this plan that the family will read what they say.

[Provider name] holds this plan under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy.

This register holds one row for every child who receives from [Provider name]. The row is the index to the child's file. It shows who the is, who is in the team, what the family agreed to, and when each , review and report was due and done.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 56 (1) to s 56 (4), s 56 (5)(a) and s 56 (5)(b).
  • Also s 57 (1) to s 57 (8), on the family.
  • Also s 58 (1) to s 58 (4), on inclusion, and s 59 (1) to s 59 (4), on collaboration.
  • Also s 60 (1) to s 60 (5), on capacity building, and s 61 (2), on practitioner skills.
  • Also s 62 (1) to s 62 (6), on outcomes.
  • Legal basis: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, Schedule 5, clauses 3 to 9. Section 20(3), item 18 of those Rules applies Schedules 1 and 5 to early intervention for early childhood.
  • No NDIS instrument sets the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the indicators.
  • Each fact is held once. The forms hold the detail and the family's words. This register holds the dates, the names, the counts, the record numbers and a one-line pointer to the form.
  • Clearances and training are in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Intake and the service agreement are in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register (Rise not yet written); until it exists, column F holds who has .
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after supports end, or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).
  • Retention where column J holds a record number: keep the row for 45 years (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; our standard). Check the child safe and records law of [state or territory] at adoption and before any row is destroyed.

Columns A to G and I are filled before the first session, and columns H and Y by the end of it. Column J stays blank until a record exists. Columns K to X and AH are filled as the plan is made and followed. Columns Z, AA and AD are filled when an interruption, a transition or an exit comes up. register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard). The Service Manager names the plan lead that day.
  2. Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each get their own row, linked in column AF.
  3. Fill columns A to G and I before the first session. Column J stays blank until a record exists. The first session does not go ahead while column I is empty for the type of setting it is in.
  4. Fill columns H and Y by the end of the first session.
  5. Fill every other column within 2 business days of the form or meeting that produces it (our standard).
  6. Write "not yet asked" with a date when a required answer is not known. Ask at the next contact with the family.
  7. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  8. Columns H, N, R, X, Z, AH, AI, AJ and AK hold dated entries. Add each new entry underneath the last one. Column AL holds one date, replaced at each check.
  9. The family's own words stay in the forms (FRM-ECS-02, FRM-ECS-03, FRM-ECS-05). This register holds dates, names, counts, record numbers and one-line pointers. Where a short phrase of the family's is entered, such as "none wanted" in column N, it is entered as it was said, signed or shown. Nobody tidies it.
  10. Column J takes record numbers only. Never write what was seen, said or suspected in this register.
  11. When the plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, the Service Manager names another worker to keep the row.
  12. When the system is down, complete the paper forms. Enter the row within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  13. A sole trader is the plan lead and keeps every row.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • column AD is filled and column AC says "exited"
  • the family has their final and their copy of the last plan
  • column AA shows the handover was given, or the family's decision that none was wanted
  • every consent line in column Q has a withdrawn date or an end date
  • nothing in column AE, AI, AJ, AK or AL is still due.
